title: Filing ITR Online: A Step-by-Step Guide for Indian Taxpayers
description: Filing your Income Tax Return (ITR) online is a mandatory annual process for most eligible individuals in India. The e-Filing portal of the Income Tax Departm.

faq.a: Individuals whose gross total income exceeds the basic exemption limit (₹2.5 lakhs for those below 60, ₹3 lakhs for senior citizens, ₹5 lakhs for super senior citizens) must file an ITR. Also, individuals with specific financial transactions, even if income is below the exemption limit, might need to file.

faq.q: What is the last date to file ITR?
faq.a: For salaried individuals and those not requiring an audit, the due date for filing ITR for a given financial year (e.g., FY 2023-24) is typically July 31st of the subsequent assessment year (e.g., July 31, 2024).

Yes, if you discover an error or omission after filing your original return, you can file a revised return under Section 139(5) of the Income Tax Act. The deadline for filing a revised return is usually December 31st of the assessment year.

faq.q: What happens if I don't verify my ITR?
faq.a: If you do not verify your ITR within 30 days of filing, your return will be considered invalid and will not be processed by the Income Tax Department. This is equivalent to not filing your ITR at all and can lead to penalties.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to link PAN with Aadhaar for ITR filing?
faq.a: Yes, it is mandatory to link your PAN with Aadhaar for filing your Income Tax Return, as per Section 139AA of the Income Tax Act. Failure to do so can lead to your PAN becoming inoperative.

The Annual Information Statement (AIS) is a comprehensive statement of financial transactions undertaken by a taxpayer in a financial year. The Taxpayer Information Summary (TIS) is a category-wise summary of information available in AIS. Both are available on the e-Filing portal and help taxpayers reconcile their financial data.
